scope: New isolated native visibility owner source/OFF-only host/selected target inspection; no native publication or hardware qualification.

result.context_lifetime: Caller-retained real NativeAdrenoMemory/table and persistent owner must outlive every returned callback. Already-held device references are accounting, not hardware stop/route proof. No rebind/reset/release/destructor cleanup.
result.table_pool_checks: Native descriptor, no imported/WC/pool backing, one span/offset0/fullbytes, nonzero real device refs, stable mapping/bytes,4KiB pages within range. Valid stable typed objects/exclusive caller gate are preconditions, not arbitrary-pointer authentication.
result.native_capture: First raw32 native error and last native result with availability/attempt index are retained separately from adapter failures. A later post-call failure preserves native SUCCESS0 as original result, never overwrites it.
result.failure_behavior: Permanent local failure latch; failed publication quarantines retained table object; reentry latches failure, no native retry or automatic cleanup. Counter overflow refuses.
result.actual_call_modes: 4096B page, writes=false/include_write_combined=false; actual raw w0 saved after return
new_host_negatives: ON host link refused without native publisher stubs
limitations: Selected callback/native error paths were compiled and statically inspected, not executed or tested with successful/failing native publishers.
Synchronous native cache publication may block. Snapshot returns Busy while a call is in flight; no cancellation/wall-time/readable-failure guarantee is claimed.
Actual context/stream/power/security/stop/route ownership remains absent. Callback binding and NativeMemory reference count do not supply it.
Caller must retain both native memory and callback owner through every possible callback. Source lifetime/range checks do not prove arbitrary concurrent or corrupted kernel memory safety.
Old NativeAdrenoSmmuMemory still uses its original binary-status callback until a separate default-OFF composition is qualified; upstream files/legacy patch remain unchanged.
